subject: radiology
title: Intravenous Urography, CT Urography and Urethrograms

steps.title: IVU follows contrast excretion
steps.tx: **Intravenous urography** films the kidneys as injected contrast is filtered and concentrated, showing a nephrogram of the parenchyma then a pyelogram of calyces, pelvis, ureters and bladder. The pictured urogram shows hydronephrosis, where dilated calyces club and the pelvis balloons above a downstream block. CT urography has replaced most IVU work, but the excretion logic still explains every delayed film the examiner shows.

steps.title: Hydronephrosis grading on imaging
steps.tx: **Hydronephrosis** dilatation starts in the renal pelvis, then blunts the calyceal fornices, clubs the calyces and finally thins the cortex in chronic obstruction. Ultrasound grades follow the same march from pelvic fullness to cortical loss. Dilatation alone does not prove obstruction, because pregnancy, diuresis and a refluxing system also fill the pelvis, so a renogram or delayed excretion phase separates plumbing from blockage.

steps.title: Spider leg and drooping lily
steps.tx: **Spider leg calyces** splay around multiple renal cysts in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, the calyces stretching long and thin between cysts on urography. Drooping lily instead describes a duplex kidney whose obstructed, non functioning upper moiety pushes the functioning lower moiety down and out like a drooping flower. Both signs name duplex and cystic anatomy from one excretion film, a favourite examiner pairing.

steps.tx: **Spider leg calyces** splay around the cysts of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, stretching long and thin between the cysts on an excretion film. The drooping lily is a different shape on the same kind of study. An obstructed, non functioning upper moiety of a duplex kidney pushes the working lower moiety down and outward, like a flower hanging over. Spider legs mean cysts. A drooping lily means duplex anatomy with a blocked upper pole. The two signs are not substitutes.
steps.say: In polycystic kidney disease the calyces become thin spider legs stretched between cysts. A drooping lily is the other urographic shape: a blocked upper moiety of a duplex kidney pushes the functioning lower moiety downward. Cystic disease and duplex anatomy should not be given each other's name.

vis.caption: Long thin calyces curve between multiple renal cysts in the pattern called spider leg calyces. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Cobra head and bladder signs
steps.tx: **Cobra head sign** is a ureterocele bulging into the bladder, contrast filling its head with a thin radiolucent halo for the sac wall. In adults it usually sits on a single system orthotopic ureter, while in children it joins the ectopic upper moiety of a duplex kidney. A bladder filling defect in the same film needs the opposite workup: clot moves, tumour stays fixed to the wall and enhances.

steps.title: MCU and RGU divide the urethra
steps.tx: **Micturating cystourethrogram** fills the bladder and films voiding, the study for posterior urethral valves, vesicoureteric reflux grading and bladder neck behaviour in children. Retrograde urethrogram instead injects from the meatus to map the anterior urethra, strictures and false passages in adult men after trauma or infection. The two studies meet at the posterior urethra, so reports state which side of it each contrast column proved.

steps.title: Staghorn and sponge kidney stones
steps.tx: **Staghorn calculus** casts the renal pelvis and branches into calyces like antlers, built from struvite laid down during infection with urease splitting bacteria such as Proteus. Medullary sponge kidney instead clusters tiny calcifications in dilated medullary tubules, painting a bunch of grapes or paintbrush blush on excretion films. Both calcify visibly on plain film, while uric acid stones stay radiolucent there and need CT or ultrasound to appear.

Medullary sponge kidney clusters tiny calcifications painting a bunch of grapes on excretion films. Uric acid stones stay radiolucent on plain film and need CT.

steps.title: Papillary necrosis ring sign
steps.tx: **Papillary necrosis** sloughs the renal papilla tip, leaving contrast to fill the cavity as a ring or lobster claw around the detached fragment. The cause list is taught as POSTCARDS: pyelonephritis, obstruction, sickle cell disease, tuberculosis, cirrhosis, analgesic abuse, renal vein thrombosis and diabetes, with systemic vasculitis completing some versions. Diabetes with infection is the commonest ward pairing, and the sloughed papilla can itself obstruct the ureter.

steps.title: HSG and testicular Doppler
steps.tx: **Hysterosalpingography** injects contrast through the cervix to outline the uterine cavity and prove tubal spill into the peritoneum during infertility workup, best timed after menstruation and before ovulation. Testicular Doppler answers the opposite emergency: absent intratesticular flow supports torsion needing theatre within hours, while increased flow with epididymal swelling supports epididymitis treated medically. Both studies change management the same day, which is why they survive every newer modality.
